messages:
Alex K. (Support): Escalation from LogiApp — they reported a big p95/p99 latency regression starting after yesterday's quantization profile update. Ticket #12345. They say p50 ok but p95 ~2x and p99 spikes up to 5-6s for chat completions. Also a few customer-reported quality dropouts. Repro steps attached below.

Alex K. (Support): Repro steps from customer: 
1) POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-phi-3-q-int8-calib (profile: int8 calibrated)
2) 1k short requests (avg tokens 40)
3) Observe latencies and occasional output truncation/strange tokens

They included curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-phi-3-q-int8-calib", "input":"Summarize: explain k-v cache"}'
```

Alex K. (Support): Logs they pasted (trimmed): 
```
[2024-06-23T14:01:02Z] request_id=abcd123 model=redwood-phi-3-q-int8-calib tokens=42 total_ms=3120 p95 spike
[2024-06-23T14:01:05Z] kernel_fallback: true fallback_from=int8_to_fp16 reason=calib_mismatch
[2024-06-23T14:01:05Z] kv_cache_miss_rate=0.03 batch_size=1
```

Sam T. (eng-runtime): Thanks Alex. Assigning this. First guess — calibration mismatch causing frequent kernel fallback which is expensive. Need: model variant, exact quant profile id, deployment region, recent deploy IDs. Also want a flamegraph or perf counters for the slow requests.

Sam T. (eng-runtime): Can you ask LogiApp whether they toggled any client-side flags (streaming vs non-streaming) and confirm the exact model name they hit?

Alex K. (Support): Confirmed: they hit redwood-phi-3-q-int8-calib in us-west-2 region. They didn't change clients, same SDK. They also said throughput was low — single request loads that reproduce higher percentile. They don't have flamegraphs.

Ana R. (eng-ml): Adding context: Our int8 calibrated builds rely on a representative calibration set. If calibration drift (different token distribution) or we trimmed calibration steps for the recent fast rollout, quantized kernels may occasionally detect out-of-range activations and trigger fallback to fp16 for safety — that causes a full-codepath change and extra kernel memcpy + dequant step which explains p95/p99 jumps.

Ana R. (eng-ml): Quick checklist: 
- Which quant profile hash was deployed (we tag them in metadata)
- Was calibration run with the customer's distribution?
- Any new cutoff thresholds (clamp thresholds) in the latest profile?

Sam T. (eng-runtime): I pulled the rollout: profile tag qprof_20240622_v3 went live at 2024-06-22T22:17 (deploy id: deploy-8794). qprof_20240622_v3 changed clamp_threshold from 7.2 -> 6.1 and enabled aggressive per-layer skipping. That could explain more fallback when activations exceed the new clamp.

Dev S. (eng-sre): From infra side — I checked the autoscaler logs and there's no GPU shortage. But I do see kernel_fallback events correlate with a single GPU thread per instance spending ~60-80% extra time in memcpy. We should capture one of those slow requests with tracing. ops-bot can capture traces if we invoke the tracer on a specific request_id.

ops-bot: Trace capture command available: `/trace capture abcd123` (background tracing enabled for prod).

Sam T. (eng-runtime): Ops-bot run that trace pls. Meanwhile, quick mitigation options: 
1) Roll back profile to qprof_20240615 (previous stable) for the affected model variant in us-west-2.
2) Add a temporary routing policy: requests with token length < 128 -> keep int8; requests >=128 -> route to fp16 variant. (If issue is activation distribution shifting with longer contexts.)
3) Disable aggressive per-layer skipping in the profile (hotfix).

Ana R. (eng-ml): Also we can attempt rapid recalibration: re-run calibration with the customer's representative prompts (they provided a small corpus). That may reduce fallback frequency. But calibration takes ~30–45 min and requires a canary rollout.

Alex K. (Support): Customer asked for immediate relief; prefer rollback if safe. They are ok with a short rollback window.

Sam T. (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a targeted rollback to qprof_20240615 for model redwood-phi-3-q-int8-calib in us-west-2 only. Canary 5% -> monitor p95/p99 for 15 minutes -> full.

Sam T. (eng-runtime): Planned commands (internal): 
```
# list deploys
rwctl deploy list --model redwood-phi-3-q-int8-calib --region us-west-2
# rollback to profile
rwctl deploy patch --deploy-id deploy-8794 --set quant_profile=qprof_20240615 --canary 0.05
```

Dev S. (eng-sre): I'll watch SLO dashboards (p95/p99) and GPU kernel_fallback counter. Also disable autoscaler scale-down during canary window.

ops-bot: Canary initiated for deploy-8794 -> qprof_20240615 at 2024-06-23T15:04Z (canary 5%).

Sam T. (eng-runtime): After 10min canary: preliminary numbers from Grafana: p50 stable, p95 dropped ~40% back to baseline, p99 down ~60%. Kernel_fallback events on canary hosts reduced to near zero. Looks promising.

Alex K. (Support): Customer reports latencies improving within minutes, can confirm p95 back to expected. They asked what we changed and whether this will recur.

Ana R. (eng-ml): Root cause hypothesis: the new qprof lowered clamp thresholds and enabled skipping heuristics that didn't align with some real-world prompt distributions — resulted in transient activation overflow detection and safe fallback. Fallback is correct and preserves correctness, but costly.

Ana R. (eng-ml): Longer-term mitigations: 
- Improve calibration dataset diversity (add LogiApp-like prompts)
- Add automatic calibration drift monitoring and alerts for fallback rate increase
- Add a preflight synthetic load test that exercises extreme tokens/lengths for each profile before rollout
- Provide a fast fallback route: instead of full fp16 fallback, support per-layer selective fp16 fallback with lower memcpy cost (longer term engine change)

Sam T. (eng-runtime): Short-term: keep qprof_20240615 as stable until we re-calibrate v3. I'll schedule a controlled recalibration using customer corpus tomorrow at 03:00 UTC in staging then canary in region.

Dev S. (eng-sre): Postmortem action items for this thread: 
- [ ] Add fallback-rate metric to model dashboards (alert if >0.5% fallback/1min)
- [ ] Add pre-deploy synthetic calibration checks to CI for quantized profiles
- [ ] Document rollback runbook for quant_profile changes (one-liner rwctl steps)

Sam T. (eng-runtime): I'll open a follow-up RFC for safer quant profile rollouts (gradual clamp change, synthetic tests).

Alex K. (Support): Thanks team. I'll reply to customer with the rollback summary and ETA for a permanent fix.

Ana R. (eng-ml): One more note — quality regressions the customer saw: likely due to partial dequantization/precision noise when fallback happens mid-sequence. We should mark any eval suites that catch those artifacts and include them in calibration checks.

Sam T. (eng-runtime): Closing loop — rolling back globally for that model in us-west-2 completed at 2024-06-23T15:32Z. Monitoring phase for 60m.

Dev S. (eng-sre): Post-canary metrics look stable. I'll file the incident in postmortems with link to ticket #12345 and join with Ana & Sam for the runbook tomorrow.

Alex K. (Support): Customer notified and very appreciative. Putting thread into follow-up for re-calibration schedule. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident logged -> INC-2024-4873 (latency regression due to quant profile).

Sam T. (eng-runtime): TL;DR for notes: quant profile change lowered clamp thresholds -> increased fp16 fallback -> p95/p99 spikes. Mitigation: targeted rollback + plan for recalibration + monitoring.

Alex K. (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll attach the runbook suggestions to the ticket.
